subject.title: macOS update can leave manual-update loop and stale node host causing Gateway restart storm

question: Should macOS `openclaw update` keep same-version package refresh as a restart-capable default, or should same-version/update-job relaunch paths become no-op/dedupe-only before touching the Gateway service?
rationale: Current tests deliberately preserve same-version package refreshes, but the field report shows that behavior becomes a restart storm when launchd keeps relaunching an updater job; choosing the default requires maintainer upgrade-policy intent.

options.title: Dedupe And Guard Restart
options.body: Keep package refresh available, but make stale/concurrent launchd updater jobs self-disable and prevent repeated Gateway stops when the target version is already installed.

options.title: No-Op Same-Version Updates
options.body: Treat same-version package updates as no-op before plugin sync and restart unless an explicit refresh or repair mode is requested.

options.title: Manual Recovery Only
options.body: Leave current refresh semantics in place and document `openclaw gateway status --deep` plus `launchctl bootout` recovery as the supported operator path.

recommendation.title: Dedupe And Guard Restart
recommendation.body: Keep package refresh available, but make stale/concurrent launchd updater jobs self-disable and prevent repeated Gateway stops when the target version is already installed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the broadest ownership across update handoff, restart sentinel, and launchd lifecycle code.
